claim: `StorageProxy` must forward `checkMutationIsPossible` before `mutate`, because the inherited `IStorage` implementation unconditionally throws.

`checkTableCanBeRenamed` must be forwarded by `StorageTableProxy`, not generic `StorageProxy`, because forwarding it generically would materialize a `StorageTableFunctionProxy` during metadata-only rename.

`checkTableCanBeDetached` should not currently be added to `StorageProxy`: `IStorage` documents the hook for dictionaries, the only real override is `StorageDictionary`, and lazy loading excludes dictionaries.
An unloaded lazy `MergeTree` can contribute no data to a backup because `StorageProxy` inherits the no-op default `IStorage::backupData`, which backup collection calls directly.
A lazy `MergeTree` exposed through `StorageProxy` currently reports false for `isMergeTree` and `supportsTTL` because those virtuals are not forwarded.
`StorageProxy` inherits `supportsOptimizationToSubcolumns`, so it can report support even when a nested engine such as `IStorageCluster` explicitly opts out.
The missing `StorageProxy::onActionLockRemove` forwarding is part of the `START` half of the action-lock incident because callers invoke it on the proxy.
A Clang AST CI check can guard `StorageProxy` interface growth by comparing all virtual `IStorage` declarations with exact `StorageProxy` overrides and requiring rationale for allowlisted omissions.

Swapping the database map entry from a `StorageProxy` to the materialized storage does not solve forwarding correctness because escaped pointers, UUID-map entries, and action-lock bookkeeping retain the proxy.

The clean long-term lazy-loading boundary is a catalog entry containing parsed metadata plus a once/future and optional real `StoragePtr`; catalog lookups materialize before returning a pointer while system metadata enumeration uses parsed metadata without a `StoragePtr`.
The `lazy_load_tables` proxy is considered unsafe for upstream promotion because it weakens type identity and has roughly sixty unforwarded virtuals, including a silent-empty `backupData` path.
The baseline `BM_Admits` promote preview is O(1) at about 1 microsecond across N, while `BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit` is O(N) at about 4.0 nanoseconds per row, reaching about 400 microseconds at N=100,000.
The baseline `BM_ReplayHistory` benchmark takes 4.93 seconds at N=100,000 and models repeated O(N) manifest-collision scans during recovery folding.
The baseline `BM_ScratchCopy` of a materialized `RefTableState` is O(1) at about 46 nanoseconds regardless of N.
The baseline `BM_SnapshotEncode` is O(N) at about 159 nanoseconds per row.
The baseline `BM_Materialize` operation is O(N log N), reaching 18,145,559 nanoseconds at N=100,000.
`RefTableState` was encapsulated as a closed class with private fields and public getters; mutation is restricted to `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `materializeCommitted`.
The E1 `TrustedHistory` replay mode reduced `BM_ReplayHistory` by about 21.6% to 23.4% across N=100 through N=100,000, but the benchmark remained O(N).
`TrustedHistory` was initially restricted to replay of transactions that had already passed `Full` validation at append time; all writer previews and append-time validation retained `Full` checking.
The E2 owned-manifest COW index changed `BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit` from O(N) to O(1), with about 720 nanoseconds at N=100,000 versus 410,636 nanoseconds in E1.

Using `std::unordered_map` for the `RefCowManifestSet` overlay increased scratch-copy cost by 37% to 42% because copying an empty unordered map allocates a bucket array; the overlay was changed to `std::map`.

The E2 owned-manifest index added about 13 nanoseconds, or 28%, to `BM_ScratchCopy` but made `BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit` flat O(1); the index also regressed `BM_ReplayHistory` to about 50,082 nanoseconds per row because its overlay grew during replay.

The shipped E3 replay optimization applies `TrustedHistory` in place with no copy and accepts a poisoned local state on throw because replay returns the state only after full success; `Full` retains the two-phase scratch-copy guarantee.
E3 reduced `BM_ReplayHistory` at N=100,000 from 4.98 seconds to 0.172 seconds, a 96.5% reduction and about 28.9 times faster.

The E4 flat-vector `RefCowMap` base was reverted because only `BM_Materialize` met the two-times target at N=100,000 while `BM_MergedIteration` improved by at most 1.28 times and `BM_SnapshotEncode` stayed within noise.
The final RefTableState experiment tree reduced `BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit` at N=100,000 from 400,222 nanoseconds to 701 nanoseconds, about 571 times faster and O(N) to O(1).

The first `TrustedReplay` validation-elision design failed open on double-owner history; the correction runs the cross-owner check unconditionally and makes snapshot duplicate-owner validation fail closed.
The corrected replay implementation deletes public `ApplyMode` and keeps poison-on-throw in a private `RefTableState::applyTxnInPlace` reachable only from `replay`.
The E5 unique-owner materialization benchmark at N=100,000 measured 13,355 nanoseconds versus 23,066,663 nanoseconds for the forced slow path, about 1,727 times faster.
The E5 soak recorded `CasRefMaterializeInPlace=81,467` versus `CasRefMaterializeCopy=14`, indicating that the in-place fast path handled 99.98% of production materializations.

The consistency soak found that GC round duration and pool growth under mutation churn were pre-existing round-cadence scaling behavior, not regressions in the F1-F11 GC-path changes; a checkpoint reduced the pool from 132 GB to 3.7 GB.

A lazy `StorageTableProxy` caused `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` to misidentify a table as not replicated after chaos recovery; the proxy must be materialized for the check, and the lazy proxy itself took about 18 milliseconds to materialize in the reproduction.
The definitive consistency soak found the main bottleneck in `CasRefLedger::appendRefOps` condition waits, with about 97,000 samples, rather than CPU; CAS CPU share was modest.
A mounted CAS disk couples all pool use, including reads, to a live mount lease and heartbeat; using the pool without them violates the mount contract.
A CAS pool directory removed while mounted caused the lease-renewal thread to raise `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and the exception constructor aborted debug and ASan builds in CI PR #2073.
A CAS disk is cached forever in the process disk registry by `Context::getOrCreateDisk`, so it has no clean teardown or runtime reset path.
A not-fully-mounted CAS disk must not be treated as erased: benign-absent answers are safe only after positive establishment of data erasure; otherwise access must fail loudly.

A full-prefix LIST can prove pool emptiness only on a backend with documented strongly consistent prefix LIST semantics and only after the required settle/grace window and repeated samples; Local, Emulated, unqualified S3-compatible gateways, and RustFS without evidence have no natural proof.
CAS disk use is through untracked `shared_ptr` holders, so `use_count` cannot reliably determine whether a disk is unused or identify who holds it.
`MergeTreeData` part loading enumerates through `iterateDirectory`; a benign-absent result on a not-live disk can silently attach an empty table over intact data.
A lease-loss callback is untyped and cannot distinguish foreign fencing, transient deadline expiry, an absent mount key with intact data, and confirmed backing destruction.
`runFsck` has no coherent snapshot and can race any node's GC; every hard finding must be revalidated against the authoritative current ref and the exact body via `HEAD` before reporting it.
The landed Dormant/UNMOUNT lifecycle is unsound because its benign-absent behavior can silently skip reclaim and make ATTACH load an empty table when data may still exist.

Lazy `ensureMounted()` from `store()` is rejected because it inverts the `lifecycle_mutex → gc_scheduler_mutex → pointer_mutex` lock order and can deadlock; a benign probe also cannot distinguish table binding from a sweep.
A sound CAS lifecycle must use typed health states, fail-loud data-bearing enumeration outside a proven `Vanished` state, and reserve benign-absent answers for `Vanished` only.
A CAS disk stop must hand pool teardown to a thread other than the keeper callback thread and serialize scheduler shutdown through `gc_scheduler_mutex`.

CA stateless retries require unique disk names as well as unique paths because the disk registry is keyed by name; `${CLICKHOUSE_TEST_UNIQUE_NAME}` and `${CLICKHOUSE_USER_FILES_UNIQUE}` are used for the test fix.
Runtime reuse of the same CAS disk after a stop is intentionally dropped; tests use unique names, and decommission is handled by configuration plus restart or `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET`.

The rev.8 lifecycle has `Running/live`, `transient-not-live`, `IdentityLost`, `Vanished(replaced)`, and `Vanished(forgotten)` states; uncertain states throw, while only operator `FORGET` or foreign-pool proof supplies truthful absent answers.

`IdentityLost` is terminal: it is entered only after authoritative `KeyAbsent` for both `_pool_meta` and the owner-claim key, the remount thread exits, matching-sentinel restoration does not revive it, and recovery requires restart or `FORGET`.
`Vanished(replaced)` is established by a single transient-recovery comparison showing `_pool_meta` present with a foreign `pool_id`.

The six CAS operation classes are Factory, Probe, ContentRead, Write, Remove, and Admin; transient and `IdentityLost` states throw for every class except Factory, while `Vanished` Probe answers absent/empty and Remove succeeds as a no-op.
The rev.8 `Vanished(forgotten)` error states that `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` decommissioned the disk, that erasure was not verified, and that a restart re-registers the name.

Before a pre-terminal or read-only enumeration answers empty at a `TableDir` or `DetachedContainer` root, it must perform one authoritative uncached `probeSentinel(_pool_meta)`; absence yields a typed throw rather than an empty result.
The rev.8 identity gate compares only `pool_id` and `blob_header_len`; successful decoding is the format gate, while `algos_used` and `min_reader_generation` are refreshed and never compared.
`ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, `Indeterminate`, and mixed probe results never produce terminal conclusions; they keep the pool transient and retry.
The GC scheduler exits at its next wake on `Vanished`, on published `vanished_intent`, and on `IdentityLost`; it does not join from a callback.
The rev.8 design permanently removes automatic erasure conclusion: a genuinely erased pool remains `IdentityLost` until an operator invokes `FORGET` or recreates it.
A 10M-row, 500-partition CAS-on-S3 INSERT measured 170.6 seconds versus 22.4 seconds for standard S3, a 7.6-times slowdown.
The measured INSERT produced `CasRefBatchFlushes=CasRefBatchedMutations=1026`, so the ref-ledger batch size was exactly 1.0, and `CasRefQueueWaitMicroseconds` was 36.2 seconds.
`2026-07-22-cas-batched-part-commit-v2-design.md` is superseded by the stage-1 internal design and a future stage-2 sink-concurrency design; it must not be implemented as written.

The production INSERT topology commits one `ContentAddressedTransaction` per part, so cross-part batching must occur at the `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` seam rather than inside `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit`.

`IDataPartStorage::takeTransactionForBatchCommit` moves out the owned transaction, returns `nullptr` for shared or inactive transactions, fires the per-part commit failpoint, and leaves `hasActiveTransaction()` false.
`IDisk::commitTransactions` defaults to the current sequential loop, so non-CAS disks retain their existing behavior and a transaction batch never spans disks.

The CAS phased engine preserves per-part `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` ordering, so the EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant remains intact while work is reordered across parts.

The phased engine uses one precommit ledger batch, one flattened cross-part upload wave, and one promote ledger batch; a 500-part INSERT is expected to reduce about 1026 serial ref-log PUTs to about two.

`submitBatch` enqueues ordinary per-item mutation records atomically but waits for all of the submitting group's items; concurrent items may join its flushes and existing same-ref and `WholeShard` carve rules remain unchanged.
If a submission group unwinds while outstanding, pending items are canceled under the queue mutex and already-carved items are awaited before teardown so their closures cannot dangle.
The v2 ref-ledger budget uses an item cap of 1000, `ref_txn_max_ops` of 5000, and a per-operation encoded-size cap of 4 KiB; normal `ref_txn_max_bytes` is removed.

When adding the next item's operations would exceed `ref_txn_max_ops`, the item and later unvalidated items are returned to the head of `pending` in order; the current flush proceeds without an exception.
An operation that exceeds the 4 KiB per-operation cap fails alone, so a pathological head item cannot cause an empty-flush livelock.

`PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` is a side-effect-free upload primitive that returns value-only results and does not mutate transaction state; upload results are merged into each part's build serially after the join.
The dedicated CAS upload pool is disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`, and its getter fails loudly when uninitialized or when the configured pool size is zero.

On a phased-commit failure, every pool task and outstanding ledger item is drained before rollback; exact rollback uses `dropRefIfMatches` and a preallocated POD outcome slot published immediately after durable promote.
`RefOp::payload` and the related `RefPayloadUpdate` API are deleted under the pre-release no-compatibility policy; `SetPayload` becomes `SetPublishedAt` with wire word `set_published_at`.
Recovery replay streams post-snapshot `RefLogTxn` objects one at a time after sorting keys by transaction ID, reducing recovery memory to O(one transaction) regardless of tail length.

`2026-07-22-cas-multicommit-phased-design.md` is superseded by the batched-part-commit v2 design and must not be implemented because its seam ownership, per-item result, leadership-exit, rollback, byte-admission, and topology assumptions were rejected.

The original phased design's byte-estimate admission was rejected because undercounting could make whole-batch `checkBudget` throw; v2 replaces it with exact operation-count admission and a per-operation size cap.

The bounded-concurrency per-part design was approved after two independent concurrency reviews, with prior blocking findings closed, but it targets the inner `ContentAddressedTransaction` commit path.

The CAS-on-S3 500-partition INSERT measured 170.6 seconds versus 22.4 seconds for standard S3, with `S3WriteMicroseconds` at 117.5 seconds, `CasRefQueueWaitMicroseconds` at 36.2 seconds, and `CasRefBatchFlushes=CasRefBatchedMutations=1026`.

A plain INSERT performs one `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit()` per part with `parts.size() == 1`, so inner-loop parallelism cannot improve INSERT; cross-part concurrency must be introduced above the disk transaction.

The approved inner-loop design dispatches each part's unchanged `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` sequence to bounded workers, preserving per-part ordering while overlapping parts.
The proposed per-part concurrency setting is `cas_commit_concurrency`, with a default of 16.
The CAS commit-worker pool must be disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; no worker may wait on work queued to its own pool.

The CAS commit pool must use bounded worker-loop callbacks or a dedicated pool sized by `cas_commit_concurrency`; scheduling one task per part on a shared 100-thread pool would not enforce the bound and could starve unrelated users.
Each worker writes rollback information into a preallocated, index-addressed per-part slot so a post-promote `bad_alloc` cannot lose a durable ref's outcome.
Worker tasks capture only non-owning transaction references, and rollback or destruction may begin only after an exception-safe join has drained every worker.
Exact rollback records `{ns, ref, manifest_id, created}` inside the serialized `appendRefOps` builder and removes a ref only when `dropRefIfMatches` still sees that exact manifest.
The first worker exception is rethrown after draining; later worker exceptions are logged and swallowed so they cannot mask the first failure.

A repoint path that abandons its scratch build must reset `st.build` after abandon or promote, because destructor re-abandonment raises `LOGICAL_ERROR` and can abort under `abort_on_logical_error` or ASan.

Concurrent part workers exposed a latent `CasRefLedger` defect: a leader throwing before carve could leave its `RefMutationItem` in `rt->pending`, allowing a follower to invoke a dangling by-reference `build_ops` closure.

After any `appendRefOps` return or throw, every `RefMutationItem` must be done or owned by a still-blocked caller; no item may remain pending for a future leader after its caller's closure state is gone.
`dropRefIfMatches` must perform its read-and-remove condition inside one `appendRefOps` builder, returning true only when the current committed binding equals the expected manifest.
`PoolConfig::cas_commit_concurrency` is planned as a `uint64` setting with default 16, while `cas_commit_pool_size` is a server setting with default 100 for the dedicated CAS commit pool.

The planned parallel commit snapshots parts into an index-addressable vector, preallocates outcome and exception slots, dispatches bounded worker loops, waits with `wait()` rather than `get()`, and performs rollback only after the inner runner scope drains.

The parallel-write validation success criterion is `CasRefBatchFlushes` much less than `CasRefBatchedMutations`, a sharp reduction in `CasRefQueueWaitMicroseconds`, and wall time materially closer to 22.4 seconds.

The phased cross-part design preserves semantic equivalence rather than byte identity: folded ref-to-manifest bindings, manifest entries, blob payloads, in-degree, and clean metadata must match, while ref-log packing, IDs, timestamps, and incarnation tags may differ.
The intra-part order `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` is an invariant corresponding to EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE and must not change under parallelization.

The initial multi-commit design used `commitTransactions` as a transaction-centric seam: generic implementations loop sequentially, while `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` groups same-disk transactions without leaking `isContentAddressed` checks into generic MergeTree code.
In the phased engine, a per-part manifest edge is durably precommitted before any of that part's blobs are uploaded, and promote runs only after all of that part's blobs are complete.
The multi-commit design uses one dedicated CAS upload pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; upload tasks return `DepEntry` values and merge them into `build->deps` only after joining.

A batch failure preserves sequential atomicity semantics: earlier members may remain committed, `renameParts` throws before Keeper block-ID registration, and rollback uses exact-manifest matching rather than inventing a new all-or-nothing promise.
`ProbeOutcome` distinguishes `Present`, `KeyAbsent`, `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, and `Indeterminate`; transport errors must never be flattened into `KeyAbsent`.

Every durable CAS PUT, DELETE, and staging finalize captures the fence generation at admission and throws typed error 668 before the backend call if mutation is no longer allowed or the generation changed; the check repeats before each conditional retry.
The CAS lifecycle operation gate defines the classes `Factory`, `Probe`, `ContentRead`, `Write`, `Remove`, and `Admin`.

In the central CAS operation gate, `Factory` is never gated; `TransientNotLive` and `IdentityLost` throw for every other class; and `Vanished` returns truthful absent/empty for Probe, typed errors for reads/writes/admin, and no-op success for Remove.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` must publish terminal intent, trip the mount fence, stop renewal without clean release unless ref lanes are drained, stop GC, join keeper/remount/GC threads outside `remount_mutex`, and then enter `VanishedForgotten`.
`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC STOP` must stop future rounds and clear `i_am_leader`; `GC START` must resume rounds on the same scheduler while preserving `gc_id`.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` must expose a non-gated lifecycle snapshot with `lifecycle`, `lifecycle_reason`, and `lifecycle_since` even when `store()` is refused for a not-live disk.
CAS FSCK must re-resolve the authoritative ref and `HEAD` the exact body before reporting a missing committed manifest; `meta_without_body` is advisory and does not make `FsckReport::clean` false.

The fail-closed CAS test teardown is `DROP TABLE <table> SYNC`, then `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET '<disk>'`, verify `vanished(forgotten)` in `system.content_addressed_mounts`, and only then remove the pool directory.

The rev.7 lifecycle plan rolls back the landed Dormant/UNMOUNT reuse lifecycle after switching tests to `DROP SYNC → FORGET → verify → rm -rf`; the abort hardening, coherent `poolAccess()` snapshot, atomic `startup()`, and `ca-fsck` rename are retained.
The parallel-write implementation plan uses `cas_commit_concurrency` default 16 and a process-wide dedicated `cas_commit_pool_size` default 100, separate from the writer pool.

The parallel-write implementation plan requires an exception-safe drain before rollback: all task handles, outcome slots, and exception slots are preallocated, and the drain waits without calling throwing `get()`.

The parallel-write plan leaves the 500-partition benchmark and BACKLOG write-path entry unresolved until `CasRefBatchFlushes` is much less than `CasRefBatchedMutations`, queue wait falls sharply, and measured wall time improves.
